title: Canonical matrix functions commute with further pullback
statement: With the normalized integral matrix data [def-weil-pbc-integral-matrix-analytic-data], the coefficient of a pulled-back finite-free map along g≫f, evaluated at z, equals its coefficient pulled back along f and evaluated at g(z). This holds for every row and column and all finite ranks.

source.place: Section 6.8, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1): integral coefficient framework and kernel-closure application; the displayed continuous-function pivot argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument written out in Lemma 6.8.7

proof.text: Use preservation of finite biproducts to move the standard inclusion and projection through the finite-free pullback comparisons. The resulting entry is conjugated pullback of the original regular endomorphism.
Apply regular-coefficient pullback compatibility twice. Both sides equal the original coefficient evaluated at f(g(z)).

proof_origin.place: Section 6.8, continuous coefficient framework; analytic matrix-chart reduction
proof_origin.note: The matrix argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument stated in Lemma 6.8.7.

lean.statement:
theorem integralMatrixFunctions_pullback (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (E : Type) [NormedField E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ] E]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y) {n t : ℕ}
    (a : Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) n ⟶
      Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) t)
    (i : Fin t) (j : Fin n) (z : Z) :
    integralMatrixPullbackFunctions ℓ E (g ≫ f) a i j z =
      integralMatrixPullbackFunctions ℓ E f a i j (g z)
